newsitem.title: UK: Salvors called out to more casualties last year.
newsitem.headline: Salvors called out to more casualties last year.

text.p: Member companies of the International Salvage Union (ISU) provided assistance to 169 vessels in 1996 compared with 141 the previous year, the organisation said on Thursday.
However, the ISU said its latest Pollution Prevention Survey showed that these operations involved the recovery of less oil, chemicals and bulkers than in 1995.
It said its members recovered 1.87 million tonnes of pollutants in 1996 compared with 2.1 million tonnes the year before.
The total broke down to 1.75 million tonnes of crude oil, 62,000 tonnes of chemicals and more than 58,000 tonnes of bunkers.

Some 20 ship-to-ship transfer operations were performed, the ISU said, with the largest involving the tankers Galp Funchal and Kraka in South African waters. Nearly 290,000 tonnes of oil was transferred from the Galp Funchal and 343,400 tonnes from the Kraka.
ISU President Arnold Witte said: "Our members were instrumental in preventing a number of major spills, which would have had grave environmental and financial consequences."
The ISU added that the oil recovery figures equated to 20 spills the size of the Braer which lost 85,000 tonnes of crude oil when it grounded off the Shetlands in 1993.
